headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress plus Unstructured’s filesystem/subprocess writes create default data-leak and conflict risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has no documented shared channel to ingest Unstructured output by default, but Unstructured can read/write files and spawn subprocesses, so a manual file bridge could carry malicious instructions. This is not a default direct bridge, so the pathway is unusual and limited. The pair is safer than a shared-MCP setup, but not provably isolated.
conditions: IF the operator copies Unstructured output into files that Airbyte later parses as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF Airbyte is configured to ingest document text from a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte and Unstructured on separate workspaces.
Disable any file-based instruction parsing in Airbyte.
Review Unstructured outputs before feeding them onward.
Use a strict schema for handoff files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data, while Unstructured reads files and can write outputs in a shared environment. Even without explicit secrets handling, a shared workspace or pipeline can move sensitive documents into Airbyte’s outbound integrations. The leakage path is plausible in default data workflows, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, document contents can flow from Unstructured into Airbyte.
IF Airbyte is connected to external destinations, any sensitive business data in those files can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate input and export directories.
Restrict Airbyte destinations to test endpoints.
Redact sensitive fields before ingestion.
Audit file permissions on the shared host.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on pipeline handoff files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and has broad egress, while Unstructured can read/write the filesystem, install packages, and spawn subprocesses. That overlap creates a realistic chance of race conditions or clobbering if both touch the same directory or mutable artifacts. Unstructured’s documented multi-instance support reduces but does not eliminate conflict risk; Airbyte’s write surface is less explicit, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, files can be overwritten or partially processed.
IF Airbyte and Unstructured share mutable state without locks, concurrent updates can conflict.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Add file locks around shared paths.
Use immutable handoff filenames.
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured produces parsed document text that Airbyte can plausibly ingest into downstream pipelines. If Airbyte treats that output as authoritative, parsing errors or hallucinated structure can cascade into bad loads or transformations. Airbyte’s business-data role makes downstream impact meaningful, while Unstructured’s document-processing role is the upstream source of error. Verification is not documented, so the safer severity is medium.
conditions: IF Airbyte consumes Unstructured output without validation, parsing mistakes propagate downstream.
IF downstream jobs act on extracted fields automatically, erroneous document structure can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Validate extracted fields against a schema.
Sample-check outputs before loading.
Keep a human approval step for critical documents.
Log source-to-destination mappings.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Airbyte touches business data and Unstructured handles documents, but there is no cited evidence of PHI, EU-only data, or conflicting policies. Because the profiles are sparse, I avoid inventing a compliance breach and keep this low rather than none due to the data-handling surface.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are routed through either agent, compliance review is required.
IF retention settings differ between the two deployments, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify data before routing.
Confirm retention settings on both systems.
Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Document the processing purpose.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
